title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
description: Explore the essential streets and corridors surrounding Cornell University, from the high-energy hubs of Collegetown to the historic pedestrian paths of downtown Ithaca.

cards.title: The Heart of Collegetown
cards.subtitle: Collegetown Corridor
cards.notes: Walk this central artery to find student staples like Collegetown Bagels and the Schwartz Center for the Performing Arts.
cards.short_summary: College Avenue is the primary commercial spine of Collegetown, serving as the main social and transit hub for Cornell students.
cards.evidence_claim: College Avenue is described as the epicenter of off-campus student life, packed with apartment buildings, restaurants, and late-night food spots.
cards.access_notes: Public street with high foot traffic; most businesses open daily from morning until late night.

cards.title: The Dining Hub
cards.subtitle: Collegetown Corridor
cards.notes: Visit this block for a high density of international eateries and the primary parking garage for the Collegetown district.
cards.short_summary: Dryden Road intersects College Avenue and is known for its diverse culinary options and dense student housing.
cards.evidence_claim: Dryden Road is highlighted as a key part of Collegetown with a variety of culturally diverse menus and the Dryden Road parking garage.
cards.access_notes: Public street; parking garage available for a fee, but walking the corridor is free.

cards.title: The Historic Gateway
cards.subtitle: Collegetown Corridor
cards.notes: Enter campus through the historic Eddy Gate at the top of this steep hill, which once served as the university's main entrance.
cards.short_summary: Eddy Street is a historic corridor featuring the original stone entrance to Cornell and long-standing local businesses.
cards.evidence_claim: Eddy Gate, built in 1896 at the top of Eddy Street, is the original main entrance to Cornell University and features the school's motto.
cards.source_title: Collegetown 101: How Ezra's University Shaped a Neighborhood
cards.access_notes: Public street; the steep incline makes it a popular but strenuous walking route to campus.

cards.title: The Gorge-Side Corridor
cards.subtitle: East Hill District
cards.notes: Walk along the edge of Cascadilla Gorge to see unique architecture, including the former residence of Carl Sagan.
cards.short_summary: Stewart Avenue runs parallel to the campus gorges, offering scenic views and historic residential landmarks.
cards.evidence_claim: 900 Stewart Avenue is a landmark building noted for its Egyptian Revival architecture and for being the residence of astronomer Carl Sagan.
cards.source_title: Riddle of the Sphinx: Carl Sagan's former home remains an intriguing local landmark
cards.access_notes: Public street; the Sagan house is a private residence visible from the sidewalk and the opposite side of the gorge.

cards.title: The Pedestrian Spine
cards.subtitle: Downtown Ithaca
cards.notes: Explore this four-block pedestrian mall for independent bookstores, local boutiques, and the Sagan Planet Walk.
cards.short_summary: The Commons is Ithaca's award-winning pedestrian district and the cultural center of the downtown area.
cards.evidence_claim: The Commons is a four-block pedestrian district serving as a daily hub for students and locals with independently owned shops and public art.
cards.access_notes: Pedestrian-only zone; open 24/7, though individual business hours vary.

cards.title: The Historic Hill Climb
cards.subtitle: DeWitt Park to East Hill
cards.notes: Climb this steep street to see historic mansions and Buffalo Street Books, a community-owned cooperative bookstore.
cards.short_summary: East Buffalo Street connects downtown Ithaca to the Cornell campus, passing through the historic DeWitt Park area.
cards.evidence_claim: East Buffalo Street is home to Buffalo Street Books and serves as a strenuous walking route that ascends from DeWitt Park toward the hill.
cards.access_notes: Public street; very steep incline between downtown and the university.

cards.title: The East Hill Plaza Hub
cards.subtitle: East Hill District
cards.notes: Head here for essential services like the P&C Fresh grocery store and various Cornell administrative offices.
cards.short_summary: Pine Tree Road is the primary commercial corridor for the East Hill area, located just east of the main campus.
cards.evidence_claim: East Hill Plaza on Pine Tree Road is a convenient suburban shopping center near Cornell with a grocery, pharmacy, and laundry services.
cards.access_notes: Public road and shopping center; accessible via TCAT bus route 82.

cards.title: The Gorge Trail Access
cards.subtitle: Cascadilla Gorge Corridor
cards.notes: Access the lower entrance of the Cascadilla Gorge Trail, which features eight waterfalls along a stone-stepped path.
cards.short_summary: This road borders the Cascadilla Gorge and provides a scenic pedestrian link between downtown and Collegetown.
cards.evidence_claim: The Cascadilla Gorge Trail creates a direct connection between Cornell University and downtown Ithaca, following the creek through waterfalls.
cards.access_notes: Public road; trail access is seasonal and typically closed during winter months for safety.

cards.title: The Student Residential Block
cards.subtitle: Collegetown Housing
cards.notes: Observe the high-density modern student housing developments that characterize the recent growth of Collegetown.
cards.short_summary: Catherine Street is a dense residential block in Collegetown known for its proximity to campus and large apartment complexes.
cards.evidence_claim: Catherine Commons and other large apartment buildings on Catherine Street offer student-focused living in the heart of Collegetown.
cards.source_title: Catherine Commons | Student Apartments Near Cornell University
cards.access_notes: Public residential street; primarily used by students walking to the nearby Engineering Quad.

cards.title: The West End Gateway
cards.subtitle: West End District
cards.notes: Visit the West End for a more local feel, featuring the Kitchen Theatre Company and the original Gimme! Coffee location.
cards.short_summary: West State Street is the main thoroughfare of Ithaca's West End, offering a mix of local businesses and cultural venues.
cards.evidence_claim: The West End, centered along State Street, is home to the Kitchen Theatre and local favorites like Gimme! Coffee, offering a genuine local flavor.
cards.source_title: Ithaca – West End Apartments - CSP Management
cards.access_notes: Public street; located about a 20-minute walk or short bus ride from the downtown Commons.
